Goose - 1 year & 29lbs, Terrier Mix, Neutered 

Want to see videos of him - please click HERE 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Our Team Says: "We get to stroll around the neighborhood with this snuggle buddy most mornings — his foster mom, who runs @elsewhereespresso, lives near our office and does the same daily community garden circuit we’re on. What a fun start to each day. As soon as Goose sees someone he recognizes, the gentle wiggles start ramping up. Even if he doesn’t know you, he’ll get excited at the chance to meet a new friend. This slight 1-year-old terrier mix (only 30 lbs) is an easy going, joyful boy. After an initial adjustment period from Tennessee pup to NYC boy, he’s proven himself potty trained, fine home alone, confident, affectionate, awesome with other dogs, a gentle treat taker, quiet, and great on leash. His only flaw, if you can call it that, is he’ll try to drag you into an alternate universe if he sees a squirrel. May not be a great match with cats, and working up to off leash activity will need to be a careful journey.
Goose needs a solid 90 minute walk each morning and is mister mellow once he’s had that exercise."

His Foster Family Says: “Goose is a sweet little cuddle bug that does well when he gets attention and a long walk in the morning. He loves to say hi to everyone and is polite with other dogs too. Occasionally he jumps on people to say hello, but we’ve been working on it and he’s been doing much better. He pulls a bit on the leash but that has also improved with some training. He hasn’t had any accidents inside the house since his second day here and now seems confident peeing and pooping outside. He is definitely interested in squirrels and cats and the occasional bird or rat, so that is something to be mindful of. Leaving him alone has so far not been a problem. Otherwise he spends a lot of time snoozing on the couch or in bed. He’s a wonderful, special little creature.”

TOLERANCE TO CITY
City boy  – Doing so well here! 

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Okay for a home with respectful children 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Nope – Chases and barks at cats etc., definitely not a good match for a home with cats or pocket pets

MOUTHY BEHAVIOUR 
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime hasn't chewed on anything and so far hasn't been interested in toys.

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Doing pretty well on leash! 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Medium – Likes to snuggle when he's in the mood but often stays in his own bed
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time
I'd say he's between medium and high. he loves to cuddle but will also have some alone time snoozing in the other room.

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Needs training – Very excited to greet everyone and has no idea how to do so politely. Jumps up on most strangers or other dogs that go by. In puppy phase or wasn’t trained as a young adult.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

pets.description: Lou - 10 years, 70lbs, Aussie/Hound Mix, Neutered Please click here if you want to see videos of Lou! Our Team Says: " Potty trained, friendly, great with other dogs, fine home alone, walks nicely on a leash, respectful of your stuff. He’s also good with gentle children, which we can rarely say with confidence. Lucious’s only crime is being a victim of divorce. This 10-year-old Aussie/hound mix was adopted from us back when he was a tiny puppy — very sadly he was recently surrendered back to us because his family is going through a tumultuous, difficult change and none of his former humans is in a position to give him the care he needs and deserves as he navigates his golden years. The good news is this handsome and polite big boy (73 lbs) is going through this major transition like a champ. He’s staying with one of our volunteers, and she hasn’t had a single complaint. In fact, all she’s done is gush." His Foster Mom Says: “Lucious aka Lou is very loving and laid-back. He seems confused sometimes, which is understandable, but he is VERY smart. He’s also very friendly and loves to say hi to other dogs (but gets bored fast). Did I mention he is cuddly? Super affectionate and likes to be around his humans. Lou is OBSESSED with his ball. As long as he has it, all is well. If the ball rolls under something, he’ll bark for it. It’s the cutest thing, he spends most of the day sleeping on the couch with that ball. He’s vocal when he wants to play fetch, go outside, or meet a pup, but he’s very responsive to training and direction. He’s also strong willed, so you just need to be clear about what you want from him. For instance, he’s great on a leash but if you give him too much freedom, he’ll pull hard. He doesn’t like tile/hard floors, maybe they are too slippery for his senior legs. While he’s quite spry for a mature dog, he only needs two medium walks and a potty break and sleeps most of the day.” TOLERANCE TO CITY City Pup - has zero issues in the city Potty trained? Yes - no issues here Social with dogs? Yes - great with other dogs Social with children? (ALWAYS requires adult supervision) Yes - previously lived with children. Okay to be in a home with kids. pets.description: River - 1 year & 28lbs, Beagle/Terrier Mix, Neutered This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Thier Foster Parent Says: " River has been so sweet, affectionate and curious since day one. He is fully potty trained, well-mannered at home, and comfortable spending a couple of hours alone. He loves meeting other dogs and people, and exploring and sniffing everything along the way. At home, he’s a total cuddle bug who loves curling up in your lap while you're working or watching TV. River is very food motivated, knows a couple commands (sit and come), and responds well to learning with treats and positive reinforcement. He enjoys long sniff walks, a little jogging with fetch, and sturdy chew toys. He has some typical puppy energy, especially around birds, squirrels, and dogs he wants to play with, but redirects easily with a treat. He only seems to be vocal in an outside setting when leaving the company of other dogs we encounter on his long walks. Crate training is still a work in progress, and he can be an enthusiastic chewer, so durable toys are a must! Overall, River has been a joy to have and is going to make a wonderful companion to someone." Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog itting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Energy level: MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY City pup – Seems unfazed by the sights and sounds, may as well have been born here. He perks up when hearing sounds and occasionally goes to look out the window, but doesn't react any other way. On walks he just tries to smell everything POTTY TRAINING Yes – Few or no accidents. River - 1 year & 28lbs, Beagle/Terrier Mix, Neutered 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Thier Foster Parent Says: "River has been so sweet, affectionate and curious since day one. He is fully potty trained, well-mannered at home, and comfortable spending a couple of hours alone. He loves meeting other dogs and people, and exploring and sniffing everything along the way. At home, he’s a total cuddle bug who loves curling up in your lap while you're working or watching TV. River is very food motivated, knows a couple commands (sit and come), and responds well to learning with treats and positive reinforcement. He enjoys long sniff walks, a little jogging with fetch, and sturdy chew toys. He has some typical puppy energy, especially around birds, squirrels, and dogs he wants to play with, but redirects easily with a treat. He only seems to be vocal in an outside setting when leaving the company of other dogs we encounter on his long walks. Crate training is still a work in progress, and he can be an enthusiastic chewer, so durable toys are a must! Overall, River has been a joy to have and is going to make a wonderful companion to someone."

Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog itting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.)

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
City pup – Seems unfazed by the sights and sounds, may as well have been born here. He perks up when hearing sounds and occasionally goes to look out the window, but doesn't react any other way. On walks he just tries to smell everything

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents. No accidents at all

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN
Hasn't really interacted with kids, on walks he sees them, walks up to them slowly and then just continues sniffing away

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc. Mostly chases squirrels and birds, hasn't interacted with cats or any other animals

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. hasn't chewed on any furniture or shoes, just is a little mouthy when giving kisses, but stops with a firm "no"

SEPARATION ANXIETY
Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time Very big cuddle bug, most days after work when we are watching tv, he calmly lays right next to either of us and sleeps or just lays there.

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

CRATE TRAINING
Working on it – We set one up and leave the door open but rarely close it because the dog freaks out Working on getting him to be comfortable in the crate, and go in on his own, we give him treats and meals in it, quickly comes out when done, he slept through the night without any whining or crying twice, but now caught on so he stays out most of the day and doesn't want to sleep in there on his own accord.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc

Adjusting to the city
Adjusting to the city pretty well. Okay to live in the city. 

POTTY TRAINING
Adjusting — uses pads and goes outside 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
In between bean – Fine with meeting new people but not particularly interested, kind of shy in busy social situations like a gathering or a packed day in the park.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Yes – Seems to get along with cats etc., either tries to play with them or is mostly uninterested

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime - he loves bully sticks

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Lower – Independent, mostly keeps to themself (may be a new rescue or shy, this could change)

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

She loves sniffing everything and taking her time investigating her surroundings. Although she enjoys exploring, she can be nervous around loud noises and sudden movements, particularly when large trucks or bicycles pass by. She is still building her confidence in the outside world, so patience, reassurance, and a gentle approach are important. She isn't the type of dog who needs to run around or play nonstop. She seems happiest enjoying a peaceful walk at her own pace, with plenty of opportunities to sniff. Nelly also gets along very well with my own dog, who came from the same rescue group in Puerto Rico. They coexist beautifully and peacefully at home, often relaxing in separate spots or taking turns enjoying the couch. She has been very respectful of his space, and I've had no issues having them together. In terms of potty training, Nelly is making progress! Submit an adoption application a[t socialteesnyc.org](http://socialteesnyc.org)

**Our Team Says:** "This pup was rescued from a hoarding situation in PR - involving about 40 dogs. Due to this these pups are on the shyer side and need patient people who will give them time to get used to normal life. They are very sweet dogs: just need more time and patience. We love these dogs - we've rescued about 15 of them and they have all been a joy."

**Thier Foster Parent Says:** "Nelly is the sweetest, gentlest girl with so much love to give! She can be shy and a little hesitant when meeting new people, but once she feels safe and comfortable, her affectionate personality really shines. One of my favorite things about her is how enthusiastically she wags her tail whenever I interact with her at home. Her little tail just keeps going left and right nonstop! She loves attention, gentle pets, and massages, and sometimes she even closes her eyes in complete relaxation while being massaged. She also likes following me around the apartment where she will quietly watch what I'm doing. She is truly a sweet soul who just wants to be loved. Nelly is a professional couch potato! She absolutely loves sleeping and can happily spend hours napping in a cozy spot. She is very calm and peaceful indoors and doesn't need constant entertainment or stimulation. When I leave home, she usually settles down and sleeps peacefully until I return. Once I'm back, she greets me enthusiastically with her adorable wagging tail! She is not an overly energetic or playful dog, and I think that is part of what makes her so special. She is perfectly content just being near her people, enjoying affection, and relaxing in a comfortable environment. Outside, Nelly is a curious little explorer! She loves sniffing everything and taking her time investigating her surroundings. Although she enjoys exploring, she can be nervous around loud noises and sudden movements, particularly when large trucks or bicycles pass by. She is still building her confidence in the outside world, so patience, reassurance, and a gentle approach are important. She isn't the type of dog who needs to run around or play nonstop. She seems happiest enjoying a peaceful walk at her own pace, with plenty of opportunities to sniff. Nelly also gets along very well with my own dog, who came from the same rescue group in Puerto Rico. They coexist beautifully and peacefully at home, often relaxing in separate spots or taking turns enjoying the couch. She has been very respectful of his space, and I've had no issues having them together. In terms of potty training, Nelly is making progress! She consistently poops outside and has also started peeing outdoors more often. However, she sometimes still prefers using a pee pad indoors. She knows exactly where the pee pad is and deliberately goes there when she needs to pee. Her habits are improving, and I believe she will continue making progress with a patient family and a consistent routine.  

Overall, Nelly is such a special girl. She may not be the most outgoing or playful dog, but she has an incredibly gentle and loving personality. She doesn't ask for much—just a safe, peaceful home, a cozy place to sleep, and someone who will give her the love and affection she deserves. Given her background, it's especially heartwarming to see her slowly discovering how wonderful life with humans can be. I think she would thrive with a patient, loving family who appreciates her calm temperament and gives her the time she needs to build confidence. She has so much love to give, and whoever adopts her will be getting a truly wonderful companion!"

**Level of dog ownership experience required:**  

BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. 

**TOLERANCE TO CITY**  

 Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue).   

  

**POTTY TRAINING**  

Yes  — Goes outside and uses pads   

  

**COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS**  

Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home.  

  

**BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)**  

Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle)

**SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS**  

Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines  

  

**RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)**  

Okay to be in a home with a cat   

  

**MOUTHY BEHAVIOR**  

Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime  

  

**SEPARATION ANXIETY** (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)  

Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.  

  

**LEASH MANNERS**  

Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.  

  

**CUDDLE BUG LEVEL**  

Lower – Independent, mostly keeps to themself (may be a new rescue or shy, this could change)  

  

**JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO**  

Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor.  

  

**CRATE TRAINING**  

NELLY - Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

**Medical status:**  

Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

**How did this dog end up with Social Tees?**  

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

Joey really is a spunky little lovebug. Don't be fooled by his age! He can be slow to warm up to some men. Joey really is a spunky little lovebug."

Very slowly, but I notice him come out of his shell tiny bits at a time more everyday. He is the easiest dog. He is fully housebroken, never barks. My parent's fostered and ended up adopting a dog a couple of years ago that is a lot like him. I think he has a long road ahead before he seems more comfortable with people, but I can already tell that in the few weeks I have had him that he is learning that I am part of his pack and trusts me. Just this morning he got out of his bed on his own and came to find me putting on my shoes because I was about to take him outside. I clipped on his leash and only slightly had to coax him to go out. Normally I have to go to his bed and pick him up or he won't go. He still is spending 100% of his time in his little bed, aside from when I walk him, but I believe in time he will join me in the other room here and there. I see the curiosity and bravery trying to push through. When we are on walks he is curious about other dogs and wants to socialize with them. He will also stop and look up at people as they walk by like he is curious about them. My husband is traveling right now so I think it is possible that he is also checking to see if any of those people are him. Like I was mentioning with my parent's dog, only now a few years later will she choose to jump on the couch and sit with me and my husband and let us pet her, and when we go home to my parent's she comes to greet us now, but that took a while. Similarly to kids, I am inclined to say that he would be good in a home with other dogs and it might help him come out of his shell a bit more. With other animals Would be fine in a home with a cat Mouthy Not at all. He doesn’t really play and has never shown any sign of aggression or a snarl or anything like that. He is fully housebroken, never barks. My parent's fostered and ended up adopting a dog a couple of years ago that is a lot like him. She would barely look you in the eyes, didn't want to be pet, would stay in her crate or bed pretty much all the time, but I watched her come out of her shell the same way Chester is. I see the curiosity and bravery trying to push through. When we are on walks he is curious about other dogs and wants to socialize with them. He will also stop and look up at people as they walk by like he is curious about them. My husband is traveling right now so I think it is possible that he is also checking to see if any of those people are him. Like I was mentioning with my parent's dog, only now a few years later will she choose to jump on the couch and sit with me and my husband and let us pet her, and when we go home to my parent's she comes to greet us now, but that took a while. He seems to have a very similar demeanor. Extremely sweet, but very cautious. I also think that a home with another dog that is trained and sweet would be really good for him. He is slowly but surely becoming acclimated to the city, however he is easily scared by noises around him. This has gotten better in the time we have had him, but I think it will be a long road for him.

Yes. The only accident was the very first day we had him (to be expected) none since then.

Comfort level with strangers
Generally speaking he is a wallflower. We have noticed that with females he seems to be more inclined to say hello if they want to engage with him. Fortunately even though myself and my husband are cis men, he has taken to us and seems to seek us for comfort in various situations.

Comfort level with kids
It is hard to say how he will be with kids as not only do we not have any, but he hasn’t encountered many on walks or in our building that he’s really gotten close to. He is SO gentle that I am inclined to say he would be good and very tolerant with kids, however it is important to know that I don’t think he would enjoy playing with kids in any way.

Social behavior with other dogs
Our building is very dog friendly so there are lots of dogs in the building and we encounter many on our walks. Similarly to kids, I am inclined to say that he would be good in a home with other dogs and it might help him come out of his shell a bit more.

With other animals
Would be fine in a home with a cat 

Mouthy
Not at all. He doesn’t really play and has never shown any sign of aggression or a snarl or anything like that.

Alone time / Separation
He is totally happy being left alone. Sadly I almost think sometimes he would prefer it, which is hard for us because our frenchie that we had for15 years was like velcro and always wanted to be around us and sitting with us, cuddling and getting pets. That said, I am of course happy he doesn’t seem at all anxious when we leave him alone.

Leash
Overall he is good on the leash. Sometimes he does pull and zig-zags around. This mainly seems to happen when he has been spooked. Otherwise he is pretty good on the leash and understands what’s happening.

Cuddles
As I previously mentioned, he is mostly disinterested with cuddling. A few times I Brough him into my lap and pet him and scratched him and I think he did enjoy it and made sure not to restrain or hold him there at all so he felt trapped, but if I stopped petting him pretty soon after he would leave to go back to his bed. He still hasn’t opted for sitting with us or staying after the pets stop. Maybe in time this will change. My parents had a foster that they adopted that shows a lot of the same behaviors and she now comes up to us when we come home and wants our pets and she will sometimes even jump onto the couch just to sit with us, which she doesn’t seem to do with anyone else. I am hoping he will get to this stage too, but I think it will take him a long time to get that comfortable with someone.

Jumping to greet
Definitely not. He isn’t looking to greet anyone. He is a shy shy shy guy

Crate training
He is totally crate trained and as previously mentioned he much prefers the crate. In fact we had to move it once while he was out on a walk and when he came back he went straight over to the corner where the crate was and waited for us to put it back in its correct spot. Once the crate was back in the normal spot he went right back in on his own and curled up in his blankets.

Similarly to kids, I am inclined to say that he would be good in a home with other dogs and it might help him come out of his shell a bit more.

**With other animals**  

Would be fine in a home with a cat 

**Mouthy**  

Not at all. He doesn’t really play and has never shown any sign of aggression or a snarl or anything like that.

**Alone time / Separation**  

He is totally happy being left alone. Sadly I almost think sometimes he would prefer it, which is hard for us because our frenchie that we had for15 years was like velcro and always wanted to be around us and sitting with us, cuddling and getting pets. That said, I am of course happy he doesn’t seem at all anxious when we leave him alone.

**Leash**  

Overall he is good on the leash. Sometimes he does pull and zig-zags around. This mainly seems to happen when he has been spooked. Otherwise he is pretty good on the leash and understands what’s happening.

**Cuddles**  

As I previously mentioned, he is mostly disinterested with cuddling. A few times I Brough him into my lap and pet him and scratched him and I think he did enjoy it and made sure not to restrain or hold him there at all so he felt trapped, but if I stopped petting him pretty soon after he would leave to go back to his bed. He still hasn’t opted for sitting with us or staying after the pets stop. Maybe in time this will change. My parents had a foster that they adopted that shows a lot of the same behaviors and she now comes up to us when we come home and wants our pets and she will sometimes even jump onto the couch just to sit with us, which she doesn’t seem to do with anyone else. I am hoping he will get to this stage too, but I think it will take him a long time to get that comfortable with someone.

**Jumping to greet**  

Definitely not. He isn’t looking to greet anyone. He is a shy shy shy guy

**Crate training**  

He is totally crate trained and as previously mentioned he much prefers the crate. In fact we had to move it once while he was out on a walk and when he came back he went straight over to the corner where the crate was and waited for us to put it back in its correct spot. Once the crate was back in the normal spot he went right back in on his own and curled up in his blankets.

**Medical status:**  

Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

**How did this dog end up with Social Tees?**  

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day at a minimum. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs.

POTTY TRAINING
Sort of — On the way and learning! May be using wee pads (is a puppy or a brand new rescue)

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello.

Social with dogs?
Yes. Some puppies are shy, others are bold, but all have the potential to be taught healthy socializing skills. It’s a huge part of raising a puppy and must be done carefully. How they interact with other dogs depends largely on how their humans help them learn to. 

Social with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
Sort of – some puppies enjoy interacting with children, others get easily overwhelmed by their energy and attention. Regardless, most puppies are not a great match for a home with kids under age 8 because they go through intense mouthy play and rambunctious phases and often accidentally hurt young kids while playing. Social with cats?
Yes. Most puppies have the potential to be friends with a cat. It’s on the adopter to know their cat’s temperament and preferences and to teach their puppy respectful manners. 

Mouthy play: 
High! All puppies go through phases where they chew your stuff and grab your hands, arms, feet… puppies naturally explore the world, play, and test boundaries with their mouths. (It also happens when they’re teething.) Their teeth are super sharp, so it can be a very painful phase for humans and other animals in the home. Proper training, outlets, and socialization are key.

Separation anxiety:
Most puppies have some level of separation anxiety as they learn to self soothe. Often they cry the first 10+ minutes at night or when they are left home alone or in a crate. Consistent training and alone time is crucial.

Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Needs training – Very excited to greet everyone and has no idea how to do so politely. Jumps up on most strangers or other dogs that go by. In puppy phase or wasn’t trained as a young adult.

CRATE TRAINING
Working on it – We set one up and leave the door open but rarely close it because the dog freaks out

Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives.

Working on this skill. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up.

pets.description: Daphne - 1 year & 19lbs, Beagle/Terrier Mix, Spayed This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Thier Foster Parent Says: "Daphne is the sweetest little girl with the cutest floppy ears, and everyone who meets her instantly falls in love! She has the most adorable way of showing her excitement, from tapping her little feet on the floor to jumping for joy (and she can jump sooo high!). She's a total cuddle bug who loves spending her days snuggled up with her people, with a few playful bursts of energy sprinkled in. She's also happy to sleep in and will patiently cuddle with her foster mom until she's ready to start the day! Daphne is incredibly affectionate and just wants to be part of whatever is going on, whether that means following her people around, giving kisses, or requesting some extra love and attention through playtime or cuddles. She's fully potty trained, very well-behaved, food motivated, and eager to please. She's still learning leash skills, but she's a quick learner with lots of potential! She also approaches other animals, including dogs and cats, with sweet curiosity, even when they aren't quite as friendly in return. Daphne is the perfect mix of goofy, loving, playful, and snuggly, and she's ready to bring so much joy to her forever family!" Level of dog ownership experience required: BEGINNER: This means we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale due to its breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. Energy level: MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY City pup – Seems unfazed by the sights and sounds, may as well have been born here. POTTY TRAINING Yes – Few or no accidents COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.) Yes – Seems to get along with cats etc., either tries to play with them or is mostly uninterested MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction. CRATE TRAINING Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

Potty trained?
Working on this skill. Puppies under 12 weeks old are often on track with their wee pad skills, but they’re too young to walk outside in public NYC areas yet because they haven’t finished their puppy vaccine series. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up.

Social with dogs?
Yes. Some puppies are shy, others are bold, but all have the potential to be taught healthy socializing skills. It’s a huge part of raising a puppy and must be done carefully. How they interact with other dogs depends largely on how their humans help them learn to. 

Social with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
Sort of – some puppies enjoy interacting with children, others get easily overwhelmed by their energy and attention. Regardless, most puppies are not a great match for a home with kids under age 8 because they go through intense mouthy play and rambunctious phases and often accidentally hurt young kids while playing. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age respectfully. 

Social with cats?
Yes. Most puppies have the potential to be friends with a cat. It’s on the adopter to know their cat’s temperament and preferences and to teach their puppy respectful manners.

Yes, few or no accidents

Wallflower - shy with strangers, takes a second to warm up to new people.

Okay for a home with kids aged 12 and up

Mostly. She tends to be neutral toward or ignore most dogs on the street, but gets curious She's still a little territorial. Not sure

Past this stage

Getting the hang of it

High

Listens to correction. She never jumps on strangers, but she does jump on the people she loves when she's excited, and she responds to "Gentle."

Yep/mostly

Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

pets.name: Milo
pets.description: Milo - 2 years, 20lbs, Chiweenie, Neutered Our Team Says: "This pup was rescued from a hoarding situation in PR - involving about 40 dogs. Due to this these pups are on the shyer side and need patient people who will give them time to get used to normal life. They are very sweet dogs: just need more time and patience. Milo needs a home with a yard - he only likes to do his business off leash and where he feels safe. He's a great walker though and not really scacred of the city, which is really awesome. Their Foster Family Says: " Milo is gradually adjusting to the city and I think he'll continue blossoming into a sweet, active dog with the support of other loving humans and canine buddies. His two greatest loves: sniffing dog pee outdoors (like REALLY huffing it) and curling up into a cinnamon roll in a pile of blankets. At home, he is mellow and observant. He likes to be in the same room as his humans, but he isn't (yet?) a snuggler and prefers his personal space. He hasn't taken an interest in toys, preferring instead to get comfy on any soft surface and watch the action around him. Outdoors, he is still a Nervous Nelly, keeping his tail tucked and remaining on high alert. He does pretty well on the leash, but if he gets spooked (shadows, rats, etc.) he will try to dart. We've had trouble getting him comfortable enough outdoors to go to the bathroom outside consistently (even with roasted chicken as his high-value reward); he typically holds it while we're outdoors and then goes on our balcony once we're home. He'd love a private outdoor space and a patient human who can continue working on potty training with him. He sleeps in a crate through the night without a peep, and does well home alone. He's a sweet, gentle dog who just needs some more time to adjust." ENERGY LEVEL Medium – Needs a daily 60-90 minute morning walk or window of quick paced exercise in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Otherwise pretty chill indoors. Also needs significant opportunities to socialize outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) TOLERANCE TO CITY Adjusting to the cit y – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs. POTTY TRAINING Yes - just needs a yard :) COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision) Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) — Hesitant around dogs on the street, typically retreats but occasionally shows curiosity RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.) Yes - okay for a home with cats, doesn't mind them MOUTHY BEHAVIOR Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.) Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house. LEASH MANNERS Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL Lower – Independent, mostly keeps to themself (may be a new rescue or shy, this could change) JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. pets.descriptionHtml:
Milo - 2 years, 20lbs, Chiweenie, Neutered

Our Team Says: "This pup was rescued from a hoarding situation in PR - involving about 40 dogs. Due to this these pups are on the shyer side and need patient people who will give them time to get used to normal life. They are very sweet dogs: just need more time and patience. Milo needs a home with a yard - he only likes to do his business off leash and where he feels safe. He's a great walker though and not really scacred of the city, which is really awesome.

Their Foster Family Says: "Milo is gradually adjusting to the city and I think he'll continue blossoming into a sweet, active dog with the support of other loving humans and canine buddies. His two greatest loves: sniffing dog pee outdoors (like REALLY huffing it) and curling up into a cinnamon roll in a pile of blankets. At home, he is mellow and observant. He likes to be in the same room as his humans, but he isn't (yet?) a snuggler and prefers his personal space. He hasn't taken an interest in toys, preferring instead to get comfy on any soft surface and watch the action around him. Outdoors, he is still a Nervous Nelly, keeping his tail tucked and remaining on high alert. He does pretty well on the leash, but if he gets spooked (shadows, rats, etc.) he will try to dart. We've had trouble getting him comfortable enough outdoors to go to the bathroom outside consistently (even with roasted chicken as his high-value reward); he typically holds it while we're outdoors and then goes on our balcony once we're home. He'd love a private outdoor space and a patient human who can continue working on potty training with him. He sleeps in a crate through the night without a peep, and does well home alone. He's a sweet, gentle dog who just needs some more time to adjust."

ENERGY LEVEL
Medium – Needs a daily 60-90 minute morning walk or window of quick paced exercise in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Otherwise pretty chill indoors. Also needs significant opportunities to socialize outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.)

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs.

POTTY TRAINING
Yes - just needs a yard :) 

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Wallflower – Very shy with new people and takes a while to warm up. Afraid when unfamiliar people try to say hi on the street, hides or shrinks back when new people visit the home.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle)

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) — Hesitant around dogs on the street, typically retreats but occasionally shows curiosity

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Yes - okay for a home with cats, doesn't mind them 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
Lower – Independent, mostly keeps to themself (may be a new rescue or shy, this could change)

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor.

CRATE TRAINING
Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night.

Medical status:
Healthy for their age as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. Adopters will need to be ready for senior care – at a minimum, that will be annual checkups including senior bloodwork and a dental post adoption (most senior rescues need one).

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc

Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. 

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60 walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

Okay in the city?
We don’t know yet because this pup is brand new to us. Most adult dogs do well in the city after they’ve had time to adjust to a new environment, but some never adapt and need homes in the burbs.

Potty trained?
Probably! Adults usually are, but all will have transitional accidents for the first week or so. A consistent walking route and schedule plus finding spots with grass or dirt can help.

Social with other dogs?
Yes, but we don’t know to what degree yet. Some like to wrestle with every passing pup, others can coexist well but prefer to keep to themselves. We’ll learn more soon.

Social with cats?
Not sure yet! Some breed mixes that are generally NOT great matches for homes with cats include large hounds, huskies, and shepherds. 

Comfortable with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)
We’re not sure yet, but we try to err on the side of caution. Respectful kids ages 8 and up are probably a safe bet. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age carefully.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?
Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

Maggie - 1 year & 15lbs, Chi/Terrier Mix, Spayed 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Maggie is a sweet 1-year-old Chihuahua/Jack Russell Terrier mix who weighs a perfectly portable 16 pounds. She was a little shy when she first arrived in foster care, but she warmed up within 24 hours and has been blossoming ever since. Maggie is a true cuddle bug who loves curling up next to her person. She’s the ultimate binge-watching buddy, ready to settle in beside you for one more episode (or five). When you come home, get ready for the best welcome of your day, because her excitement is impossible to resist. But don’t let the couch potato side fool you. Maggie is just as happy to get outside, soak up some fresh air and help you get your steps in. On walks, she has a little prance in her step that will make you smile, and she’s the kind of companion who makes every lap around the block feel like an adventure. She gets along great with her foster siblings, Addy, a 50 lb dog, and Socks, a 12 lb cat, and she’s fully house-trained with zero accidents. Maggie takes her job as head of household seriously. She’s devoted to her person. She’ll do best with an adopter who can give her patience, consistency and lots of love. Once she knows she’s yours, you’ve got a loyal sidekick for life."

Level of dog ownership experience required:
BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. 

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60 walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs.

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
In between bean  – Fine with meeting new people but not particularly interested, kind of shy in busy social situations like a gathering or a packed day in the park. 

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Maybe for age 12 and up – Is either big and energetic (okay with kids big enough not to get knocked down) or a little skittish (could be comfortable with older children that can be extra gentle) 

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) 

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Yes – Seems to get along with cats etc., either tries to play with them or is mostly uninterested. Currently living with a cat. 

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction. 

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Listens to correction – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

CRATE TRAINING
Yep/mostly – Seems comfortable in the crate, may whine a little at first but settles pretty quickly. We use the crate when we leave the pup alone and/or at night. 

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses.

Working on this skill.** Puppies under 12 weeks old are often on track with their wee pad skills, but they’re too young to walk outside in public NYC areas yet because they haven’t finished their puppy vaccine series. Puppies older than 12 weeks are usually learning to do their business outside. Potty training takes a lot of patience, consistency, and clean up.

**Social with dogs?  

Yes.** Some puppies are shy, others are bold, but all have the potential to be taught healthy socializing skills. It’s a huge part of raising a puppy and must be done carefully. How they interact with other dogs depends largely on how their humans help them learn to. 

**Social with children?  (ALWAYS requires adult supervision)  

Sort of** – some puppies enjoy interacting with children, others get easily overwhelmed by their energy and attention. Regardless, most puppies are not a great match for a home with kids under age 8 because they go through intense mouthy play and rambunctious phases and often accidentally hurt young kids while playing. Children must always be monitored and taught to interact with dogs of any age respectfully. 

**Social with cats?  

Yes.** Most puppies have the potential to be friends with a cat. It’s on the adopter to know their cat’s temperament and preferences and to teach their puppy respectful manners. 

**Mouthy play:   

High!** All puppies go through phases where they chew your stuff and grab your hands, arms, feet… puppies naturally explore the world, play, and test boundaries with their mouths. (It also happens when they’re teething.) Their teeth are super sharp, so it can be a very painful phase for humans and other animals in the home. Proper training, outlets, and socialization are key.

**Separation anxiety:**  

Most puppies have some level of separation anxiety as they learn to self soothe. Often they cry the first 10+ minutes at night or when they are left home alone or in a crate. Consistent training and alone time is crucial.

**Leash manners:**  

None or learning, depending on the puppy’s age. Will need to work on this skill. 

**CUDDLE BUG LEVEL**  

**High** – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

**JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO**  

**Listens to correction** – Only jumps on people they know when really excited, stops with correction.

**CRATE TRAINING**  

**Working on it** – We set one up and leave the door open but rarely close it because the dog freaks out

Medical status:  

Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.)

How did this dog end up with Social Tees?  

Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. 

PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. 

This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes.

He’s incredibly friendly and affectionate and will happily stop on walks to say hi to pretty much everyone he sees!

He is mostly potty trained  - might have a few transitional accidents while getting used to a new home.

He can get very excited when new people come over and may jump up to say hello, but it’s purely because he’s so happy to meet people and be loved.

Jagger walks well on a leash, although he does have some typical little-dog zigzagging and likes to stop and investigate things along the way.

Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org THEIR FOSTER SAYS: "Bear is exactly what his name suggests: a big, lovable teddy bear who would happily spend his days curled up next to you (or on top of you!) simply because he doesn't quite realize how big he is. He is the ultimate cuddle bug and will gladly rest his big head in your lap whenever he gets the chance. And if you get close enough, you're officially in the face-kissing zone! When he isn't asking for cuddles, you'll usually find him curled up like a little donut on a soft bed or couch, enjoying one of his many naps. At night, he loves sleeping right by your side, and in the morning, he's more than happy to roll over for belly rubs. In fact, if you approach him while he's relaxing, don't be surprised if he immediately flops onto his back, belly up, asking for scratches. He also loves having his floppy ears cleaned and his coat brushed, and he's very comfortable being handled. One thing to keep in mind is that he can be a little nervous around blow dryers and other similar loud noises. On the other hand, he's an expert traveler and does wonderfully in the car, even on longer drives, happily settling in for the ride. Bear is also a very quick learner, especially when treats are involved! He's already picked up several commands, including sit, lay down, place, and paw, and his recall continues to improve every day. With his eagerness to learn, he'll likely continue making great progress with consistent training. He's also an incredibly curious guy who loves exploring his surroundings, whether that's sniffing every corner of your apartment or investigating interesting spots along his walks. He even enjoys looking at his own reflection! Outside, he loves bird-watching and gets especially curious whenever he spots one nearby and his hunting instincts kick in. Although he's three years old, Bear can sometimes act like a giant puppy, especially when he's outside! He's a true social butterfly and has been fantastic with dogs of all sizes and ages. He's incredibly friendly with both people and other dogs and is always excited to meet new friends. He especially LOVES playing with his furry friends, particularly those around his own size who can keep up with his playful energy. Bear truly thrives outdoors. He loves rolling around in the grass, soaking up the sunshine, and simply watching the world go by. At home, however, he's a much more relaxed guy who spends most of his day napping. That doesn't mean he doesn't enjoy keeping his mind busy! He loves brain games, learning new tricks during training sessions, chewing on his favorite bones, and playing with his beloved stuffed toy, "Happy Capy" (a capybara). Happy Capy goes just about everywhere with him. Bear carries him around, takes naps with him, and treats him like his very own emotional support toy. Bear is happiest when he's surrounded by love and affection, and he would likely enjoy having another furry sibling in the home to keep him company. Of course, he'll never turn down extra belly rubs, attention, or a cozy spot next to his favorite person!Overall, Bear is a sweet, affectionate, goofy, and loving companion with so much love to give. He's the perfect combination of playful outdoor adventurer and relaxed indoor cuddle bug. If you're looking for a big teddy bear with an even bigger heart, Bear might just be your perfect match!" SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS: Yes: Gets along well with dogs of different sizes and ages and enjoys playing with canine companions. This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Bruno is the sweetest, most gentle giant. We think he might have some Great Dane in him because he is happiest laying on the couch all day or on his humans receiving pets and love. When he’s forced to get up, he happily follows you outside and does a great job interacting with the elements in NYC. He's very friendly with other dogs of all shapes and sizes and loves playing with them. He plays a little bit with toys inside, but he’s slightly awkward and walks carefully on non-carpeted floors. He's also a little skiddish of new places/stores and needs a nudge to explore new stores but he’s making progress quickly. It also took him a couple of days to get used to apartment stairs, but he has now mastered them. He’s a very tall lanky boy so it’s probably just a function of his size, but once he trusts you he follows you everywhere no matter what. He is very agreeable and comfortable with all touch including wiping paws after walks and baths. He is great on walks and follows direction really well, but needs to be guided or held close on busy streets since he takes up so much room! He figured out how to go potty outside immediately so no worries of accidents here. He also eats very well, but isn't particularly food motivated which is nice since he’s so tall (no counter surfing here!)Bruno is an amazing, once in a lifetime pup!"

Level of dog ownership experience required:
INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.)

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

City pup – Seems unfazed by the sights and sounds, may as well have been born here.He’s something in between adjusting and city pup. He is doing really well in the city but there are some things he’s still getting used to like loud loud noises or going into stores/coffee shops. But once he’s inside the apartment the street noises don’t bother him and he doesn’t get too bothered by large crowds.

POTTY TRAINING
Yes – Few or no accidents

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Yes for most ages – very confident, gentle, low energy, tolerant, not mouthy
He could totally be a nanny dog he’s so sweet.

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Yes – Good with most other dogs (sizes, breeds, etc.) as far as we know and enjoys socializing with other canines

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Probably yes but we haven’t interacted with cats. He doesn’t get bothered by or want to chase pigeons.

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Past this stage– Little to no interest in chewing on stuff or putting things in their mouth that aren’t food. Doesn’t try to chew on hands, feet, etc. during playtime

SEPARATION ANXIETY
Past this stage – Completely fine being left home alone. Doesn’t cry or exhibit destructive behavior when you leave the apartment or house.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Calm Greetings – Doesn’t jump up on people or dogs. Always all four on the floor.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

Bianca - 1 year & 12lbs, Chi Mix, Spayed 

This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application at socialteesnyc.org

Thier Foster Parent Says: "Bianca is the sweetest, most cuddly girl and always wants affection. She's obsessed with snuggling, so loving, and so happy to be safe and have a home. She loves playing with her friend Diva, loves to go in the park and sniff forever, and is obsessed with sticks and bones - stuffed animals, not so much. She's getting adjusted to using concrete for the bathroom and def prefers Washington Square Park. A very sweet girl."

Level of dog ownership experience required:
BEGINNER – “Beginner” doesn’t necessarily mean easy as all dogs will require time, work, and patience, but we predict this dog will be low on the challenge scale because of their breed/age combo. Potentially a good fit for someone who has relevant dog care experience (fostering, dog sitting) and is looking to adopt their first pup. 

Energy level:
MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) 

TOLERANCE TO CITY
Adjusting to the city – Spooked easily by loud noises and bustling areas but walks pretty well in quiet areas and probably just needs more time to adjust (may be a puppy or a brand new rescue). Would prefer a home in a calmer part of the city or the suburbs.

POTTY TRAINING
Sort of -- On the way and learning! May be using wee pads (is a puppy or a brand new rescue) -getting adjusted to using concrete for the bathroom, def prefers Washington Square Park

COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS
In between bean – Fine with meeting new people but not particularly interested, kind of shy in busy social situations like a gathering or a packed day in the park.

BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN (always requires adult supervision)
Haven't seen her with kids yet, so unsure

SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS
Mostly – Generally good with other dogs but may be selective (scared of big dogs or plays too rough for small dogs, for example) - loves playing with her friend Diva!

RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS (cats, small pets, etc.)
Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc.

MOUTHY BEHAVIOR
Working on it – Is respectful of hands, feet, etc. but likes to chew on things they’re not supposed to like shoes, furniture, etc. - learning not to nip fingers, otherwise only chews her bones

SEPARATION ANXIETY (Please leave your foster dog home alone every day for at least 20 minutes.)
Adjusting – Might cry for a few minutes when you first leave the house but settles pretty quickly and has no problem being left alone otherwise.

LEASH MANNERS
Getting the hang of it – Probably hasn’t been on a leash much in their life but figuring it out. Might be a mild puller but responds to correction.

CUDDLE BUG LEVEL
High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time - obsessed with snuggling!

JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELLO
Needs training – Very excited to greet everyone and has no idea how to do so politely. Jumps up on most strangers or other dogs that go by. In puppy phase or wasn’t trained as a young adult.

CRATE TRAINING
Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.

Medical status:
Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake

Yes – Few or no accidents

Social butterfly – Wants to be friends with everyone who walks by, loves anyone who will stop to say hello.

Not sure – Wants to chase squirrels and birds so may not be a good match for a home with cats, rabbits, etc.

High – Wants to be in your lap pretty much all the time

Not at all – Don’t even have one, I’ve puppy proofed and we free range.
